products.name: Linkurious Enterprise
products.description: Cloud SaaS and self-hosted graph-powered decision intelligence platform for relationship discovery, pattern detection, and investigation workflows. Supports Neo4j, Amazon Neptune, Azure Cosmos DB, Memgraph, and Google Spanner Graph. Acquired by Nuix (€20M, Apr 2026).
products.positioning: Enterprise fraud/compliance investigation platform with graph visualization and ML-powered anomaly detection.

products.name: Graphistry GPU-Accelerated Visual Graph Analytics
products.description: GPU-accelerated platform for large-scale graph visualization and analytics. PyGraphistry Python library for Jupyter notebooks and data science workflows. REST/Python/JavaScript APIs. Integrated with Elastic Stack.
products.positioning: Data science platform for GPU-powered analysis of million+ node graphs. Python-first for data scientists.

products.name: Kineviz GraphXR
products.description: Browser-based interactive graph visualization platform with 2D and VR capabilities for relationship discovery and pattern analysis. GraphXR Lite free open-source version. Used for cybersecurity threat analysis, ransomware tracking, and relationship mapping.
products.positioning: VR-enabled graph visualization for cybersecurity analysts and threat intelligence teams.

products.name: Cambridge Intelligence KeyLines
products.description: Low-level JavaScript SDK for embedding interactive graph visualization in custom applications. Provides layout algorithms, styling, and interaction controls. Perpetual and subscription licensing.
products.positioning: Embedded visualization library for ISVs and enterprises building custom graph applications.

products.name: Cambridge Intelligence ReGraph
products.description: React component library for graph visualization and interaction. Modern developer-friendly API built on React patterns. Perpetual and subscription licensing.
products.positioning: React-native graph component for developers building modern web applications.

products.name: yWorks yFiles
products.description: Comprehensive diagramming and network visualization SDK supporting multiple platforms (Java, .NET, JavaScript, Web, iOS). Founded 1996. Perpetual royalty-free licensing. Includes automatic layout algorithms, styling, and interaction.
products.positioning: Enterprise-grade visualization SDK for diagram and network applications across all platforms.

products.name: yWorks yEd
products.description: Free desktop graph editor for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Supports manual graph creation, layout algorithms, and export. Single-user, offline-first tool.
products.positioning: Free graph editing tool for ad-hoc visualization and layout experimentation.

products.name: Gephi Desktop
products.description: Open-source graph visualization and analysis platform (GPL). Desktop application for network exploration, layout, and analytics. Used extensively in academic research (10,000+ citations).
products.positioning: Open-source academic platform for network science and graph analysis.

products.name: Gephi Lite
products.description: Web-based open-source version of Gephi. Browser-accessible graph visualization without installation. GPL license.
products.positioning: Free browser-based graph visualization for quick exploration and layout.

products.name: Tom Sawyer Perspectives
products.description: Low-code graph visualization and analytics platform with React web client. Founded 1992. Provides declarative configuration for building custom graph applications with minimal code.
products.positioning: Low-code platform for building enterprise graph visualization applications.

products.name: Graphileon
products.description: Low-code platform for building graph visualization applications and interactive dashboards. Includes database connectivity (Memgraph, Neo4j) and dashboard building tools.
products.positioning: Low-code graph dashboard and application builder for data engineers.

products.name: Graphlytic
products.description: Graph visualization and analysis platform built on Cytoscape.js. Provides Neo4j integration, analytics tools, and automation features for relationship discovery and pattern detection.
products.positioning: Neo4j-focused graph analytics platform for relationship discovery and anomaly detection.

products.name: GraphAware Hume
products.description: Enterprise graph analytics and visualization platform with visual query builder and real-time pattern detection. Mission-critical reliability for fraud/compliance investigations and relationship mapping.
products.positioning: Enterprise mission-critical platform for graph analytics, pattern detection, and relationship discovery.

competitors.wedge_vs_them: MetroGraph focuses on intuitive HCI with metro-map visualization and AI+UI parity for graph exploration; Linkurious emphasizes decision intelligence and pattern detection but suffers from surface-area bloat in UI (20+ panels, deep config). Win on ease of use for data engineers; they win on ML-powered anomaly detection and investigation workflows. Differentiate on 'graph visualization that doesn't require training' and real-time collaborative query building.
they_win_on: Multi-database support (Neo4j, Neptune, Cosmos, Memgraph, Spanner)
Global enterprise support + Nuix acquisition leverage
we_win_on: Simplicity: metro-map-style reduces cognitive load vs. dense node/edge UIs
AI + UI parity: AI co-pilot that never breaks the visual paradigm
Smaller surface area: fewer panels, deeper focus tools
competitors.moat: Enterprise relationships (Nuix), domain expertise in fraud/compliance, acquired user base, RBAC/audit for regulated markets

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Graphistry dominates on GPU acceleration for massive graphs (100k+ nodes) but is overly technical (Python-first, REST API-heavy). MetroGraph targets data engineers who want interaction without coding. Win by offering: native browser-based exploration (no Python knowledge needed), metro-map layouts that scale elegantly, and real-time collaboration. Position as 'Graphistry's UX replacement—same power, human-centered instead of data-scientist-centered.'
they_win_on: PyGraphistry Python integration (Jupyter notebooks, pandas DataFrames)
we_win_on: No coding required: click-and-explore vs. notebooks
Metro-map layouts: intuitive hierarchical visualization vs. force-directed hairballs
Team exploration: built-in collab vs. single-user notebooks
Generalist data engineers: accessible to non-PhDs
competitors.moat: Proprietary GPU rendering tech, data science community adoption, enterprise partnerships

competitors.wedge_vs_them: GraphXR excels at 2D/VR visualization but targets cybersecurity/intelligence analysts (ransomware tracking use cases). MetroGraph targets SQL/noSQL startups and data engineers. Win by: deeper DB connectivity (Cypher, GQL, SQL dialects), no VR overhead simplifying UX, collaborative team workflows. GraphXR is analyst-tool; MetroGraph is data-team platform.
they_win_on: Browser-based (no install) with GraphXR Lite free version
we_win_on: Broader database support (SQL, NoSQL, graph DBs)
competitors.moat: VR/3D tech, cybersecurity domain expertise, free Lite version attracting analysts

competitors.wedge_vs_them: KeyLines is a low-level JavaScript SDK—requires significant frontend engineering (30% JS overhead vs. MetroGraph's no-code visual builder). They're positioning as 'embedded library' for vendors; MetroGraph competes as end-user product. Win by: offering faster time-to-value (visual builder > SDK setup), collaboration out-of-box, and managed infrastructure (no self-hosting). Niche away by offering 'KeyLines-like power, spreadsheet-like ease.'
they_win_on: Established SDK with years of investment
we_win_on: No frontend dev required: visual builder vs. JavaScript code
Faster deployment: days vs. months of integration
competitors.moat: Enterprise integrations, deep tech debt making competitors painful to swap, layout algorithm IP

competitors.wedge_vs_them: ReGraph is React SDK (modern developer experience) but still requires integration work. Position MetroGraph as 'ReGraph + collaboration + visual builder.' Win on: zero-config deployment, real-time team workflows, AI-powered suggestions, data engineer friendliness (SQL/Cypher first, not React props first).
we_win_on: No React knowledge required: visual builder for teams
Built-in collab (not DIY via state management)
competitors.moat: React developer community, component library ecosystem

competitors.wedge_vs_them: yFiles is the 'enterprise incumbent'—stable, feature-complete, but legacy (founded 1996). Minimal development/investment. MetroGraph wins by being purpose-built for graphs (not generic diagram SDKs), modern UX, cloud-native, and AI-augmented. Position as 'the yFiles replacement for 2025+'.
they_win_on: Perpetual licensing (lower TCO for large orgs)
we_win_on: Modern UX: doesn't feel 20 years old
Data team ICP (not enterprise software teams)
competitors.moat: Large incumbent customer base, switching costs, perpetual license revenue

competitors.wedge_vs_them: yEd is a free desktop graph editor—single-user, no collaboration, no DB connectivity. Not a direct competitor. Use to understand yWorks' market positioning. No wedge needed; they're orthogonal.
competitors.moat: Existing free user base, yWorks ecosystem lock-in

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Gephi is open-source, academic, desktop-focused (Java). No cloud, no team collab, no real-time DB sync. It's a one-off analysis tool (load, layout, export), not a platform. MetroGraph competes on: team workflows, real-time data, SaaS accessibility, database integration. Gephi attracts academics; MetroGraph attracts data teams.
competitors.moat: Academic credibility, open-source community, network science domain expertise

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Gephi Lite (web version) is more accessible than desktop but still lacks DB connectivity and collab. Free tier may attract users; position MetroGraph as 'Gephi Lite + real database integration + team features.'
competitors.moat: Open-source community, free model attracting price-sensitive users

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Tom Sawyer is low-code (uses declarative config, not fully no-code like MetroGraph). Founded 1992, legacy but still active. Position MetroGraph as 'Tom Sawyer but with modern UX, real-time collab, and AI-augmented query building.' Wedge: data engineers prefer clicking to config files; MetroGraph is visual-first.
competitors.moat: Legacy customer relationships, low-code reputation, industry presence

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Graphileon is low-code, cloud-based, and includes dashboards (broader scope). Good product but less specialized in graph-centric UX. Position MetroGraph as: 'graph visualization + query building focused (not general dashboards),' metro-map layouts, team collaboration, AI-assisted. Win on depth in graph exploration vs. breadth in dashboards.
they_win_on: Low-code dashboard builder (broader than just graphs)
we_win_on: Deeper DB support (SQL, Cypher, GQL variants)
competitors.moat: Low-code platform, dashboard ecosystem, Memgraph partnership

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Graphlytic uses Cytoscape.js as rendering backbone (open-source), adds analytics/automation on top. Lower barrier to entry (Cytoscape base), Neo4j-focused. MetroGraph wins on: metro-map-style layout (vs. force-directed), team workflows, real-time collab, AI assistance. Position as 'Cytoscape for teams + AI.'
competitors.moat: Cytoscape.js dependency (switching costs), Neo4j community integration, automation features

competitors.wedge_vs_them: GraphAware Hume is modern, purpose-built for graph analytics, visual query builder, real-time capabilities. Closest competitor to MetroGraph vision. Differentiators: metro-map layouts (vs. traditional node/edge), simpler UX (fewer panels/modes), AI+UI parity (MetroGraph co-pilot never breaks visual paradigm). Win by being 'Hume for data engineers' (not just analysts)—easier to learn, faster to query.
they_win_on: Visual query builder (similar to MetroGraph vision)
we_win_on: Simpler UX: metro-map reduces cognitive load vs. dense node/edge
AI+UI seamlessness: suggestions never break visual paradigm
Broader DB support (SQL, Cypher, GQL variants)
competitors.moat: Neo4j ecosystem trust, enterprise deployments, visual query builder IP, mission-critical branding

notes: Phase C extraction for graph-db-viz-platforms leaf (12 core products + 2 yWorks variants). All 12 in-scope products mapped to existing companies in the database. Feature scoring (20-25 features per product) focused on differentiation: graph exploration, layout, data connectivity, query building, governance, and UX. Competitor analysis emphasizes MetroGraph's wedge (metro-map HCI, AI+UI parity, collaborative real-time) vs. incumbents (Linkurious, Graphistry, Hume—high threat), mid-tier (Kineviz, Cambridge Intelligence, Tom Sawyer, Graphileon, Graphlytic—medium threat), and legacy/orthogonal (yWorks, Gephi—low threat). All source citations include T0 (official), T1 (docs/GitHub), T2 (reviews/analysts) references per tier authority in sources.json."
